title: Gene trajectory inference for single-cell data by optimal transport metrics

nodes.text: GeneTrajectory infers trajectories of genes (rather than trajectories of cells) by computing optimal transport (Wasserstein) distances between gene expression distributions over a cell-cell graph to extract gene programs and define their pseudotemporal order.
nodes.evidence: we present GeneTrajectory, an approach that identifies trajectories of genes rather than trajectories of cells

nodes.text: When multiple uncorrelated processes co-occur in the same cells, cell pseudotime learned from collective genes becomes uninformative because it mixes effects of multiple processes, so organizing cells into unidimensional lineages is inappropriate.
nodes.evidence: cell pseudotime learned by organizing cells using the collective genes becomes less informative, as it mixes the effects of multiple processes

nodes.text: Unlike cell trajectory approaches, GeneTrajectory dissects gene programs directly from the whole transcriptome without requiring initial cell trajectory construction or specification of initial and terminal cell states for each process.
nodes.evidence: eliminating the need for initial cell trajectory construction or the specification of the initial and terminal cell states for each process

nodes.text: Gene expression is normalized into a probability distribution over cells, and the graph-based Wasserstein-p distance is computed between gene distributions using shortest-path (graph) distances on a kNN cell graph as the transport cost (p=1 is Earth Mover's distance).
nodes.evidence: we normalize the expression of a gene into a probabilistic distribution over cells and then compute the Wasserstein distances between gene distributions in the cell graph

nodes.text: The graph-based Wasserstein distance accounts for cell geometry (higher cost to transport to distant cells) and prevents transport across ambient cell space, avoiding a problematic issue of spatial distance measures like Euclidean distance.
nodes.evidence: It prevents the transport across the ambient cell space, which is often a problematic issue when using spatial distance measures (for example, the Euclidean distance in the cell space)

nodes.text: Gene-gene Wasserstein distances are converted to affinities and embedded via diffusion map; gene trajectories are extracted sequentially by selecting the gene farthest from the embedding origin as a terminus and diffusing mass through a random-walk thresholding procedure, iterating after removing assigned genes.
nodes.evidence: we convert pairwise gene–gene Wasserstein distances into gene–gene affinities and use diffusion map... we assign a unit point mass to that gene and then diffuse the mass to the other genes

nodes.text: Genes along a trajectory are ordered by recomputing a diffusion map on only those genes and using the first nontrivial eigenvector as the intrinsic gene ordering.
nodes.evidence: The obtained first nontrivial eigenvector of the diffusion map embedding provides an intrinsic ordering of the genes along that trajectory

nodes.text: Two acceleration strategies make pairwise gene Wasserstein computation tractable on large cell graphs: cell graph coarse-graining and gene graph sparsification.
nodes.evidence: we have designed two strategies to accelerate the computation based on (1) cell graph coarse-graining, and (2) gene graph sparsification

nodes.text: Prior single-cell uses of optimal transport quantified dissimilarity between pairs of cells or cell populations (for cell distances, cell trajectories, spatial reconstruction, multi-omics integration), whereas GeneTrajectory distinctively defines the graph-based Wasserstein distance between pairs of genes.
nodes.evidence: we distinctively define the graph-based Wasserstein distance between pairs of genes to study their underlying pseudotemporal dynamics

nodes.text: In simulations of cycling and branching processes, and of mixtures of two concurrent independent processes (differentiation plus cell cycle), GeneTrajectory deconvolved the mixture into separate gene trajectories with gene ordering in high concordance with ground truth.
nodes.evidence: our approach deconvolves the original mixture of two processes into two gene trajectories... genes are ordered in high concordance with the ground truth

nodes.text: GeneTrajectory accurately extracted progressive gene dynamics in human myeloid lineage maturation.
nodes.evidence: GeneTrajectory accurately extracts progressive gene dynamics in myeloid lineage maturation

nodes.text: GeneTrajectory deconvolved key gene programs underlying mouse skin hair follicle dermal condensate differentiation that could not be resolved by cell trajectory approaches.
nodes.evidence: GeneTrajectory deconvolves key gene programs underlying mouse skin hair follicle dermal condensate differentiation that could not be resolved by cell trajectory approaches
